ErrorAnalysis.Title: Only one date is read and validated
ErrorAnalysis.Detail: The problem requires reading nine integers representing three dates and printing three results. Your code reads only three integers and prints only one line, so it does not solve the full task.
FailingScenarios: Input: 1 31 2024 2 29 2024 4 31 2024 -> expected 3 output lines, but this program handles only the first date.

ErrorAnalysis.Title: Early return stops processing remaining dates
ErrorAnalysis.Detail: If the first month is invalid, the program prints INVALID and exits immediately. In this problem, each of the three dates must be classified independently, so one bad date must not prevent checking the others.
FailingScenarios: Input: 13 1 2024 1 1 2024 2 29 2024 -> expected 3 lines, but this program would stop after the first INVALID.

ImprovementSuggestions.Title: Process all three dates
ImprovementSuggestions.Detail: Read all nine integers or loop three times reading m, d, y, then run the same validation logic for each date and print one result per date.
ImprovementSuggestions.ExpectedImpact: Makes the program match the required input and output format.

ImprovementSuggestions.Title: Remove the early program exit for invalid month
ImprovementSuggestions.Detail: Instead of returning from main when a month is invalid, print INVALID for that date and continue to the next date.
ImprovementSuggestions.ExpectedImpact: Ensures every date is classified, even if an earlier one is invalid.

ImprovementSuggestions.Title: Extract validation into a helper function
ImprovementSuggestions.Detail: Create a function such as int isValidDate(int m, int d, int y) that returns 1 for valid and 0 for invalid. Then call it three times.
